curriculum.lesson_evidence: Music can give ideas for movement. Listen to the beat, tempo, pitch and dynamics and choose movements that match the mood. Slow, soft, low music might suit smooth, low, heavy movements, and fast, loud, high music might suit quick, sharp, high movements. You can also choose to move against the mood on purpose, as long as you can explain why. Move in a clear, safe space at a comfortable volume and listen for any pause or change in the music that tells you to change.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Imagine music that is fast, loud and high. Describe the body shapes, level, speed and energy you would use to match it.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Quick, sharp jumps and hops at a high level, with arms stretched out and a bright energy.' These choices match the fast tempo, loud dynamics and high pitch, so the dance and music feel connected.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that dancers must always move exactly the way the music sounds. Dancers can choose different responses as long as they give a reason, and silence or contrast can be just as powerful.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Choose two pieces of music with different moods. For each, write the tempo, dynamics and mood, then plan movements for each using body, space, time and energy. Perform them or draw a picture of each, and say how the movement matches the music.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.
